newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy deputy PM sees budget ready before elections.
newsitem.headline: Italy deputy PM sees budget ready before elections.

text.p: The Italian government will introduce its planned mini-budget before local elections due on April 27, deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni was quoted as saying by Ansa news agency on Friday.
"A serious government, such as this one, doesn't wait for local elections before introducing budget adjustments," Veltroni was quoted as saying.

Italians newspapers reported rumours on Friday that Prime Minister Romano Prodi was considering delaying the introduction of potentially unpopular budget measures until after next month's mayoral and council elections.
Veltroni said the budget would be finalised as soon as first quarter accounts were released.
"If it seems we have to do a budget of 14 trillion lire we will do it. If we need to do a budget of 16 trillion lire we will do it, even 18 trillion lire," Veltroni said.

He added that the government's prime objective was to cut the state deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), as demanded by the Maastricht Treaty for aspirant members of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
He repeated a previous pledge that if the centre-left government failed to bring Italy to EMU, it would resign. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
